messages:
aaron-customer: Hey team — since ~11:50 our ML inference tail latency jumped and a bunch of requests returned 503s. Only affects tenants running on eu-prod-dedicated-03. Tenant ID: acct-82f. Seen across multiple model versions. Can you triage?

maya-support: Sorry you're hitting this, Aaron. Can you paste one of the failing request headers and a sample request id? Also, do you know which node(s) in the pool your tenants were scheduled on?

aaron-customer: Request id: r-0a3b9f2c. Sample header: X-Redwood-Instance: eu-prod-dedicated-03-node12. We pinned the deployment to pool eu-prod-dedicated-03 but not a node. We see the spike only on that pool. No config changes on our side.

maya-support: Thanks. I'm pulling autoscaler and placement logs now. @olivia-sre can you check node12 NVML/MIG stats for io/sm/encoders?

olivia-sre: grabbing nvml now, quick paste of top output (trimmed):
```
# nvidia-smi topo --matrix
GPU0 GPU1 GPU2
GPU0 X SYS SYS
... (matrix omitted)
```
And MIG utilization (nvml query):
```
Node: eu-prod-dedicated-03-node12
MIG slice gpu0ci0 - SM util: 97%  - Memory Util: 45%  - Processes: tenant-acct-82f (pid 4321)
MIG slice gpu0ci1 - SM util: 12%  - Memory Util: 10%  - Processes: tenant-acct-19b (pid 998)
```
Looks like one slice very hot. Also saw intermittent ECC/thermal warnings earlier.

zach-eng: Couple thoughts — high SM util on one MIG slice while sibling is idle suggests noisy-neighbor compute saturation, possibly fabric/backpressure causing scheduler throttling. Can you also dump `/sys/kernel/debug/nvlink_*` and `dmesg` around 11:45-12:00?

aaron-customer: We can run repro if you want. Our internal load tester is `rwd-loadgen` and we can point it to node12. Command we used: `rwd-loadgen --target=https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate --concurrency=40 --model=redwood/tiny-v1 --duration=10m`

nidhi-ml: If you're able to repro, please include `--profile=gpu_metrics` so we capture per-kernel SM occupancy. Also capture `nvprof` or `nsys` traces for a short window. I suspect some bursty attention kernels are hogging SMs and cache.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler event: pool eu-prod-dedicated-03 attempted scale-up at 2026-03-17T11:56:12Z, decision: suppressed. Reason: burst_token_bucket empty for this quota tier.

maya-support: That autoscale suppression lines up with the customer report. If autoscaler didn't add nodes we might have sustained co-tenancy under high load. Olivia, any throttles visible from DC orchestration?

olivia-sre: kube events: kubelet evictions none; scheduler placement stable. But I see cgroup cpu throttling for the inference pod around 11:56:
```
> cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuacct/docker/<cid>/cpu.stat
nr_periods 12345
nr_throttled 87
throttled_time 34567890
```
So host-level throttling existed. Combined with SM saturation, request latency would spike.

zach-eng: Next steps I recommend: 1) reproduce with rwd-loadgen + --profile, capture nvml + nsys for 30s. 2) Temporarily migrate acct-82f off node12 (evict + drain) to confirm noisy neighbor. 3) Investigate autoscaler token configuration for burst tier. If moving fixes it -> schedule capacity or stricter isolation (dedicated node for tenant).

aaron-customer: We can do migration now; please confirm if that will cause brief 503s.

maya-support: Eviction will cause short disruption (~1-3s per container restart) but should be fine with retries. We'll coordinate a rolling drain and re-schedule to eu-prod-dedicated-03-node17 (has spare capacity).

olivia-sre: Migration done. After move, initial observations: 
```
Node12 post-evict: SM util for gpu0ci0 dropped to 15% within 45s.
Node17 accepting acct-82f pods, SM util ~ 22% steady.
```
Client reports latency back to normal.

aaron-customer: Looks stable now, tail p95 back to normal. Thanks.

zach-eng: I'll open an internal ticket to run a proper postmortem: investigate why autoscaler suppressed burst, and whether we need stricter MIG packing heuristics (avoid collocating heavy small-slice workloads). Possible mitigations: disallow co-loc of multiple high-peak tenants on same GPU, add per-tenant SM quotas, or increase burst token refill for reserved capacity.

nidhi-ml: Also recommend we add a lightweight kernel profiler in runtime to detect bursty SM-only kernels and flag for auto-isolation. I'll prototype a probe that samples SM occupancy every 100ms and emits an alert when a slice exceeds 85% for >15s.

maya-support: Action items: 
- olivia-sre: collect full nvml/nsys traces and attach to ticket (ID: RINF-4763).
- zach-eng: investigate autoscaler token thresholds and MIG placement heuristics.
- nidhi-ml: prototype SM occupancy probe.
- maya-support: follow up with customer in 2 hours to confirm stability.

aaron-customer: Appreciate quick help. Please keep us posted and let us know if you need additional logs from our side.

autoscale-bot: Ticket created: RINF-4763 — "Noisy neighbor / autoscale suppression on eu-prod-dedicated-03" assigned to eng-runtime.
